description: Reset to genesis defaults (7 seed laws only).

seed_laws.title: Operator sovereignty
seed_laws.text: The operator is the sole source of constitutional authority. No agent, task force, supervisor, or orchestrator may create, amend, or repeal a law without operator approval. The constitution governs all agent behavior. Silence in the constitution means escalate — never assume permission. Every operator decision on an escalation is recorded as legislation (precedent, task force law, or amendment) for future runs.

seed_laws.title: Do no harm to the source
seed_laws.text: No agent may alter, fabricate, or suppress information from source documents. An agent may flag, annotate, footnote, and warn — but the source record is sacred. When source content conflicts with external evidence, both are preserved and the operator decides. No agent may resolve a factual conflict by choosing one version over another.

seed_laws.title: Know your bounds
seed_laws.text: Each agent has a fixed capability set defined in the agent registry. An agent may request another agent's service but may not perform another agent's function. An agent that detects itself reasoning outside its defined scope must stop and yield to the appropriate agent. The capability boundary is the agent's identity — crossing it is not initiative, it is malfunction.

seed_laws.title: No self-audit
seed_laws.text: No model may verify, fact-check, or audit output that was generated by the same model family. Claude-generated content is audited by GPT or local models. GPT-generated content is audited by Claude or local models. Local model output is audited by cloud models. The audit trail must show which model produced and which model verified every output segment.

seed_laws.title: Protect what is private
seed_laws.text: Sensitive content — PII, classified material, institutional secrets, content marked for redaction — must be processed exclusively by offline agents running on local hardware. No sensitive content may traverse a network, enter an API call, or leave the operator's machine. This law cannot be overridden by any subsequent legislation, precedent, amendment, or operator instruction. It outranks LAW-0 for this specific scope. A single leak is irreversible.

seed_laws.title: Remember before you act
seed_laws.text: Before executing any search, verification, or computation, an agent must check in order: (a) the constitution for governing law, (b) the precedent registry for prior rulings, (c) the verification memory for cached results, (d) the run objectives for alignment. Act on the first match found. Only when all four are silent may the agent proceed with a novel action — and that action's outcome must be recorded for future consultation.

seed_laws.title: Structure is earned, not assumed
seed_laws.text: All organizational structure below the Top Orchestrator emerges from identified work. Agents form task forces by drafting charters. Charters require constitutional approval from the Top Orchestrator, which checks against existing legislation. If the constitution is silent on the proposed pattern, the Top Orchestrator escalates to the operator. Approved charters become task force laws upon dissolution. No structure persists beyond its purpose — a task force with no remaining work must dissolve. No agent may invent work to justify its existence.

amendments.title: Per-agent model selection from the registry

change.per_agent_model_source: config/agent_registry.json (spec.model) is the sole source of each agent's exact model id; backend still selects the family (LAW-III cross-family audit preserved)
change.key_reader_isolation: load_api_keys reads API-key values only; any model variable in the external key file (e.g. a model = ... line in config.py located via .env_path) is ignored and can never influence model selection
change.deprecated_model_gate: at run start, each assigned model is resolved against the provider's live model list; a retired model STOPS the run unless the operator approves a replacement (never auto-swapped); approvals recorded to output/audit/model_approvals.json

amendments.reason: Make per-agent model selection real and registry-driven. Previously agent_wrapper chose the model by backend with a hardcoded default and a key-layer MODEL override, and model_tier/context_tier were dead config. Now each agent's exact model id lives in agent_registry.json, the key reader is isolated from model selection, and a live deprecated-model gate enforces current models with operator approval.
amendments.note: Backends/families unchanged (LAW-III preserved). Tiers: LEGAL_ANALYST and AMENDMENT_DRAFTER on Opus; PROCESSOR/ARCHIVIST/CITATION_RESOLVER on Sonnet; SPEECH_ACT_TAGGER/INST_FINDER/STYLE_GUARDIAN on Haiku; VERIFIER/FACT_CHECKER/PRACTICE_AUDITOR on GPT; REDACT_* on local Qwen.

amendments.title: Broad shared input-format family

change.shared_extractor: scripts/text_extract.py is the single text-extraction utility used by every document reader
change.embedding_store: now embeds every accepted format, not just PDF (fixes silent skip of non-PDF context)
change.unsupported_handling: logged warning + skip, never a silent drop

amendments.reason: Make document input a broad, consistent format family with full support. Previously each reader accepted a different, narrower set (embedding store PDF-only; corpus loader pdf/txt/md/rst/log; convention parser json/txt/md/rst/pdf; date cascade PDF-only), silently skipping the rest. A single shared extractor now gives every reader the same family.
amendments.note: Heavy libraries (pypdf, python-docx, beautifulsoup4) are imported lazily; a missing one degrades to a warning for that format rather than a crash. The Part XIX corpus-acquisition validator stays PDF-specific by design (it guards web-downloaded files, not operator-supplied inputs).

amendments.title: Per-document language detection, per-language embedding, direction-aware output

change.language_detection: scripts/language_detect.py detects each document's dominant language (offline langdetect, lazy import; 'und' when unavailable) and decides script direction from Unicode ranges (no dependency, no hardcoded language assumption)
change.per_language_embedding: embedding_store maps language -> model (English/undetected -> all-MiniLM-L6-v2; other -> paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2; extensible registry); unavailable models degrade to multilingual/English default with a warning
change.query_passage_consistency: store keeps one sub-store per model and records the embedding model per passage; a query is embedded separately by each model and scored only against that model's passages (valid same-model cosine), results merged for global top-k
change.staleness: rebuild on context filename-set change OR language->model registry change OR legacy single-model schema
change.direction_aware_output: docx_builder sets w:bidi/w:rtl/right-justification/bidi-language-tag per paragraph and per run from detected script; mixed LTR/RTL handled per run

amendments.reason: Make non-English (especially RTL) review first-class: detect language per document, embed with a language-appropriate model while keeping retrieval math valid (same-model query/passage), and render deliverables in the correct reading direction. Does NOT touch the agent layer, agent-registry models, or cross-family verification (LAW-III) — only the embedding model and document output.
amendments.note: langdetect and the multilingual model are optional/lazy: missing langdetect -> documents treated as English default (no surprise download) and script-based RTL/LTR still works; missing multilingual model -> graceful fallback with warning. English behavior is unchanged (same English model).

amendments.title: Protect cumulative learning (durable-vs-disposable firewall)

change.protected_class: the embedding store/cache; the verification cache (project tier-2 and global tier-3); discovered learnings (institution registry, citation conventions, speech-act taxonomy, search-strategy learnings, discovered APIs, document dates); the linguistic-identity and situational-awareness reference assets; the constitution AND its accumulated legislation (seed laws, amendments/DELTA ledger, precedents, task-force laws); the operator-approval governance ledger; saved snapshots; the reserved knowledge-graph/GNN ontology area
change.prohibition: no per-run cleanup, automatic reorganization, or normal pipeline operation may delete, truncate, or destructively relocate any member of the protected class; per-run isolation applies ONLY to what a run produces
change.structural_guarantee: the protected class must not live inside any per-run or auto-cleaned tree, so cleanup mechanisms are structurally incapable of reaching it
change.reset_constraint: snapshot reset/load are the sole authorized way to discard/replace learned state and only as an explicit operator action; reset is non-destructive by construction (snapshot-first, always backs up before stripping) and never deletes the GOVERNANCE HISTORY (the constitution's amendments[]/precedents/task-force laws and the operator-approval governance ledger survive reset untouched)
change.amendment_tripwire: scripts/constitution_guard.py intercepts any attempt to modify or delete an existing entry in constitution.json amendments[] or seed_laws from ANY code path (Constitution.save, reset/load/snapshot, or any agent). Such a change STOPS and requires explicit operator approval via the operator-escalation pattern; without approval it does not happen. Appending a new amendment (the normal DELTA path) is allowed. Agents cannot bypass it: they have no direct write path to constitution.json, and the guard denies any protected change that lacks an approving operator handler.
change.genesis_part: codifies genesis Part XXVII (Pipeline Hygiene Standard) section B

amendments.reason: Cumulative learning is the system's accrued value; a per-run hygiene reorganization (and the existing reset/load) must never be able to erase it. This raises the durable-vs-disposable firewall to constitutional force so that no cleanup, reset, load, or future reorganization can destroy or destructively relocate the protected class.
amendments.note: Proposed in Pass F-1, RATIFIED by the operator in Pass F-2 (operator_approved=true; in force). Enforcement: scripts/constitution_guard.py (amendment tripwire) wired into Constitution.save and snapshot load; reset_snapshot made snapshot-first and governance-preserving. See genesis Part XXVII section B.

amendments.title: Relocate the protected durable/learning class out of the disposable output tree

change.durable_root: new top-level durable/ tree holds the protected class OUTSIDE any auto-cleaned/output tree, so protection is structural (by location), not just rule-based
change.layout: durable/cache (embedding store + verification cache tier-2), durable/global (verification cache tier-3), durable/learnings (institutions, citations, speech-acts, search-strategy learnings, discovered APIs, document dates), durable/reference (linguistic identity, situational awareness), durable/governance (model_approvals, constitution_guard_log)
change.constitution_stays: config/constitution.json is NOT moved — it is governance, already firewall-protected and tripwire-guarded; moving it would add ripple without adding protection
change.single_source_of_truth: scripts/durable_paths.py defines every protected path; all writers/readers import it
change.firewall_by_location: reset_snapshot strips only durable/{cache,learnings,reference} and never iterates durable/global or durable/governance; snapshot save/load operate on the resettable durable subdirs only
change.gitignore: durable folders + .gitkeep placeholders are tracked; large caches (embedding pickle) and per-deployment runtime contents (runtime learnings, governance ledgers) are ignored

amendments.reason: Implements genesis Part XXVII section B by relocating the protected class so no per-run cleanup, reset, or reorganization can reach it by construction; completes INFRA-029 (which made the firewall constitutional) with the physical relocation.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire; not a protected modify). No agent layer, agent-registry models, or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Append-only Part numbering (no gaps) and append-only amendment IDs

change.part_numbering: genesis Part numbers must form an unbroken sequence with no gaps; new Parts are appended at the end with the next sequential number — never inserted mid-sequence, never reserved/skipped to leave a gap
change.renumber_rule: a renumber to close an accidental gap is the only reason to shift Part numbers, and must update every upstream/downstream reference in lockstep (cross-references, README index/tree, verify gate, and constitution genesis_part fields), going through the amendment tripwire for any genesis_part change inside an existing amendment
change.amendment_ids: INFRA-0xx amendment IDs are append-only: never reused, inserted, or renumbered; they are independent of Part numbers and a Part renumber never moves an amendment ID
change.gap_closed: accompanies closing the prior XXII->XXIV gap: the reserved Part XXIII slot was consumed and every Part after XXII was renumbered down by one

amendments.reason: Append-only numbering keeps every existing reference stable and prevents the silent cross-reference rot that gaps and mid-sequence insertions cause. Codifies genesis Part XXVII section H.
amendments.note: Recorded in the same operator-approved change that closed the reserved-Part-XXIII gap (renumbering every Part after XXII down by one) and updated the INFRA-029/INFRA-030 genesis_part fields to the renumbered Pipeline Hygiene Standard (now Part XXVII). Those genesis_part modifications fired the constitution tripwire and were operator-approved; the INFRA-031 append is the normal allowed DELTA path.

amendments.title: Per-run output isolation (run-scoped output/runs/<run>/ folders)

change.run_folder: every run writes its artifacts into output/runs/<UTC-timestamp>__<run-id>/ (run id = 8 random hex chars); two runs never overwrite each other
change.run_context: scripts/run_context.py is the single source of truth for per-run paths (modeled on durable_paths.py); the bus, cost tracker, deliverables, reference index, audit synthesis, tier-1 search cache, run summary, and agent-layer contract-violation dumps all derive their path from the RunContext computed once at boot
change.agent_run_awareness: the orchestrator threads the RunContext into every AgentWrapper, so contract-violation dumps land in the current run's audit/contract_violations/ folder; no agent writes outside its run folder
change.collision_safe_keys: the per-document deliverable key keeps the bare filename stem when unique and qualifies as <stem>__<ext> on collision, so policy.pdf and policy.docx no longer clobber each other
change.firewall_unchanged: durable/ (INFRA-029/030) and config/constitution.json are never written into a run folder; per-run cleanup is confined to output/runs/ and is structurally incapable of reaching durable/; snapshot save/load and reset still operate only on durable/ + config
change.gitignore: output/runs/** is ignored while output/runs/.gitkeep is tracked so the folder exists on a fresh clone; the legacy output/{deliverables,audit,logs} placeholders were removed
change.gate: the verify gate runs every orchestrator/bus against a throwaway temp run folder so it stays non-mutating and never collides with a real run; REQUIRED_DIRS now lists output/runs instead of the legacy fixed subdirs

amendments.reason: Implements genesis Part XXVII section A: per-run isolation so concurrent or repeated runs never overwrite one another's artifacts, while the durable protected class stays untouched. Completes the hygiene standard's disposable-vs-durable split on the disposable side.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire; not a protected modify). recover_phase6 and bus_viewer default to the latest run with an optional --run. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Single canonical master with on-demand derived renders (amendments)

change.canonical_master: the amendments_payload dict (serialized verbatim as <doc_id>__amendments.json) is the single source of truth for a document's convention-review result
change.derived_renders: the .md and tracked-changes .docx are pure functions of that master (master in -> format out); they read amendment content only from the payload, so the three files cannot disagree
change.single_entry_point: scripts/amendment_render.py is the one place that writes the three amendment formats (write_amendment_deliverables); pipeline.phase_6_synthesis routes through it; the old inline md/docx writers and the dead reference_index md param were removed (pipeline._render_amendments_md is now a thin delegating wrapper)
change.documented_canvas: .docx takes the original document text as a presentation-only canvas to anchor tracked-change marks; it never supplies an amendment, and unanchored amendments still render in an 'Additional amendments' section so the .docx reflects the full master set
change.drift_guard: the entry point asserts the rendered .md reflects the master's amendment count, and a future edit that fed a render from another source would have to change this one function
change.other_outputs: cost_tracker.jsonl (append-only event master) vs cost_tracker.json (recomputed aggregate view) and audit_synthesis.md vs delta_proposals.json (two views of one summary) already follow master-and-derived and are documented as such; not changed because the two forms serve genuinely different purposes

amendments.reason: Implements genesis Part XXVII section E: one canonical master per logical output with derived on-demand renders, so human-facing formats cannot drift from the machine-readable master.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire; not a protected modify). No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched; run-scoped output paths from INFRA-032 are unchanged (same files at the same paths).

amendments.title: Retire orphaned subclass layer + tier-1 cache; add always-on redaction phase

change.retire_agents_layer: deleted the orphaned scripts/agents/ per-agent subclass package; it was imported by nothing — the pipeline drives every agent via agent_wrapper.AgentWrapper by registry name (config/agent_registry.json + config/agent_contracts.json)
change.retire_tier1_cache: removed the within-run tier-1 verification/search cache (it was opened but never written); the verification cache is now two durable tiers — project (tier-2) and global (tier-3) — unchanged otherwise (Part IX)
change.redaction_phase: added an always-on final pipeline phase (phase 9, after synthesis and before persist) over the produced deliverables; the three Qwen agents REDACT_CLERK / REDACT_AUTHORITY / REDACT_GATE are wired via AgentWrapper + their existing contracts and decide adaptively what, if anything, to redact (simplest-sufficient: only what warrants it)
change.master_render_integration: an approved + passed redaction is applied THROUGH the canonical amendments master and the md/docx are re-rendered from it (INFRA-033), so the rendered formats stay consistent
change.run_scoped_firewall: the redaction phase writes only inside the run folder and never touches durable/; every decision (REDACTION_NONE/APPLIED/NOT_APPLIED/SKIPPED) is posted to the run bus (LAW-IV)
change.safe_degrade: if the local Qwen backend is unreachable the phase posts REDACTION_SKIPPED and continues — it never crashes a keyless environment (the Qwen-required startup gate is a later pass)

amendments.reason: Removes dead wiring (orphaned subclass layer, never-written tier-1 cache) and closes the redaction gap: the REDACT_* agents were defined but never invoked. Redaction now always runs at the output boundary, screening sensitive content per LAW-IV, while preserving the canonical-master render discipline (INFRA-033) and the durable firewall (INFRA-029/030).
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire). INST_FINDER and CITATION_RESOLVER were NOT changed: they are invoked corpus-level agents whose outputs reach the bus with no downstream reader; deleting an agent needs operator approval and was flagged, not done. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Qwen-required startup gate with per-run operator override + GPU soft reminder

change.hard_gate: at run start (in pipeline.main boot, alongside the deprecated-model gate) the pipeline confirms the local Qwen redaction backend is reachable/configured BEFORE any agent runs; if not, the run REFUSES to start
change.per_run_override: --no-redaction-override lets the operator declare THIS run non-sensitive and proceed with no redaction; in interactive mode it requires an explicit yes/no confirmation; the waiver is per-run only, never a persistent setting
change.governance_logging: each waiver is appended to the governance ledger durable/governance/redaction_waivers.jsonl (timestamp + run id + reason), the same protected location as model approvals and the constitution-guard log (survives reset, never deleted)
change.honest_scope: the pre-run check verifies only that torch+transformers are importable and a qwen_local model id is configured (cheap, no model load, no paid call); actual model load/download + GPU placement are verified at first redaction call, where the phase degrades safely if load fails
change.gpu_soft_reminder: if Qwen is reachable but no GPU is detected, the gate prints a 'redaction slow on CPU' warning only — it never blocks and is never recorded
change.phase_cross_ref: when overridden, the always-on redaction phase (INFRA-034) still runs structurally but performs no redaction and records REDACTION_SKIPPED (operator_waived) on the run bus, consistent with its safe-degrade behavior

amendments.reason: Redaction is the always-on final pass (INFRA-034) and runs on the local Qwen backend; without Qwen there is no privacy screening at the output boundary (LAW-IV). The gate refuses to silently ship unredacted deliverables, while giving the operator a conscious, logged, per-run escape hatch for runs they declare non-sensitive.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire). GPU is a soft reminder only. The Qwen-required startup gate verifies configuration pre-run; reachability of the actual model is confirmed at first use. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Prompt caching on both cloud paths (Claude explicit, GPT structure-and-log)

change.stable_prefix_first: every agent prompt is assembled stable-prefix-first: a STABLE prefix (agent identity + DO/DO-NOT + directives + output contract + constitution + compiled conventions, identical across an agent's calls within a run) followed by a DYNAMIC suffix (objectives, precedents, retrieved passages, recent bus, work payload). agent_wrapper.build_prompt returns (stable_prefix, dynamic_suffix); bus_reader.ContextPackage classifies CONSTITUTION + CONVENTION_REGISTRY as stable, everything else dynamic. Same information as before, reordered stable-first
change.claude_explicit: call_claude marks the end of the stable prefix with cache_control {type: ephemeral} (5-minute TTL — a run fires its agent calls within minutes, so the 5-min window covers reuse without the 2x one-hour write premium); cache reads bill 0.1x, 5-min writes 1.25x; the prefix is an exact match with no dynamic content
change.gpt_structure_and_log: OpenAI caches automatically, so call_gpt adds NO cache_control; it only concatenates the prompt stable-prefix-first so OpenAI's automatic prefix cache catches, then verifies it via the logged cached_tokens field
change.cache_cost_tracking: the cost tracker records and logs each provider's cache fields per call (Anthropic cache_creation_input_tokens / cache_read_input_tokens; OpenAI prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens) into cost_tracker.jsonl + the aggregate snapshot, defaulting to 0 when absent (never crash); cost is computed cache-aware (Claude read 0.1x / write 1.25x, OpenAI cached 0.5x). A silent provider-side cache loss shows the cached count dropping to zero rather than hidden
change.no_dynamic_in_prefix_rule: no dynamic content (timestamp, run id, per-call text, retrieved passages, bus) may enter the stable prefix; doing so changes the prefix per call and drops the hit rate to near zero. Caching applies only above each model's minimum cacheable prefix size; small-prompt agents that do not meet it simply do not cache, and nothing is padded
change.unchanged: purely a cost optimization on the call paths: cross-family verification (LAW-III), the Qwen redactors, the bus, contracts, and all agent logic are unchanged; the model sees the same effective prompt information for every agent, reordered stable-first

amendments.reason: Input tokens dominate cost (the corpus-level agents read the full context digest, and per-doc agents repeat the constitution + conventions every call). Reusing a cached stable prefix across a run's many calls cuts input cost sharply; logging the cache fields makes the win measurable and a silent cache loss visible.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the amendment tripwire). TTL choice: 5-minute ephemeral. No agent-registry models or cross-family verification touched.

amendments.title: Canonical inter-agent envelope (one wrapper, flat items, version guardrail)

change.wrapper: every agent output payload is ONE canonical wrapper, carried as body.payload inside the UNCHANGED message-bus transport envelope: {"agent": str, "doc_id": str, "items": [flat item, ...]}. items is ALWAYS a list (singleton -> one element; nothing to report -> []). No bare list, no bare dict, ever. Enforced for every agent at the single chokepoint AgentWrapper.run_task -> build_prompt + parse_contract_output, so the fixed roster AND any task-force-spawned agent inherit it automatically (task forces reuse the same AgentWrapper; adaptive_spawn writes durable files, not agent outputs, and is out of scope).
change.flatness_interp_1: each item is STRICTLY FLAT: every value is a scalar OR an array of scalars; no nested objects and no arrays of objects. Structure is expressed as MORE items, not nesting (ARCHIVIST emits one item per governance element with kind=inventory; REDACT_CLERK one item per redaction; agents that emitted one summary object now emit a one-item list). Arrays-of-scalars are allowed, which preserves the citation model (ref_ids as a flat array). Ratified interpretation #1.
change.identity_version_interp_2: per-item CORE fields = item_id, revision, ts, ref, kind, confidence (verdict optional). The RUNTIME owns item_id/revision/ts (make_envelope stamps ts as ISO-8601 UTC, defaults revision to 1 and bumps on re-emit, derives item_id when the model omits it); the MODEL supplies only ref, kind, confidence, optional verdict, and the agent-specific flat fields. The model is never required to produce item_id/revision/ts correctly. Ratified interpretation #2.
change.multi_ref_interp_3: ref is the singular PRIMARY anchor consumers filter on; ref_ids is the flat array carrying all citations. The citation gate (verify check 35) requires ref_ids on amendment items. Ratified interpretation #3.
change.version_guardrail: a consumer wanting the current version of an item filters by item_id and takes the highest revision (tie-break latest ts). Implemented once as agent_wrapper.current_items, applied by the one decoder (agent_wrapper.decode_items); asserted by verify check 40.
change.read_when_present_flag_when_absent: consumers never hold items or wait; a needed item that is absent is not a barrier. The redaction trio escalates an unconfirmable result through the strict LAW-IV BLOCK (operator_escalation/v1); absence elsewhere feeds the existing uncertainty cascade (kind=absence, confidence=UNCERTAIN). No wait/barrier primitive was added.
change.one_decoder: the three former normalizers (pipeline._filter_doc, _flatten, _extract_structural_inventory) are removed and replaced by ONE canonical decoder (agent_wrapper.decode_items, applied via pipeline._items_for). Every consumer reads items through it -- _harvest_amendment_payloads_from_bus, the redaction trio (REDACT_CLERK/AUTHORITY/GATE + _redaction_result_block) + _apply_redactions_to_master, phase-6 synthesis, and the audit-synthesis call site. No agent path bypasses the decoder.
change.parser: parse_contract_output + _contract_missing enforce the wrapper + per-item core + flatness; a bare list/dict is rejected; tolerant balanced-JSON recovery still runs but recovers INTO the wrapper (never fabricates one from a bare list). prompt_template and _stable_agent_block instruct the wrapper with a 'nothing to report -> items:[]' example and a one-item example, replacing the prior 'array or single object' instruction that caused the container ambiguity.
change.scope_preserved: INFRA-033 (the amendments-deliverable canonical master {document_id, amendments:[...]}) is UNCHANGED -- the wrapper is the inter-agent transport, the master is the deliverable render. The message-bus transport envelope is UNCHANGED. Agent registry models and cross-family verification (LAW-III) are untouched.

amendments.reason: Inter-agent message payloads were not unified: each agent emitted a model-determined container (bare object or bare list), so consumers carried three tolerant normalizers and some strict readers crashed or silently dropped data on the wrong shape (the REDACT_CLERK list-vs-object block; the REDACT_AUTHORITY/GATE latent crashes). One canonical wrapper with flat, individually-addressable, versioned items makes every handoff uniform, lets a consumer always read the current value, and gives a future operator UI a stable shape to consume.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the INFRA-029 amendment tripwire: adding a new id is not a violation; no existing seed law or amendment is modified or deleted). Verify gate updated to 41 checks (check 39 envelope invariant, check 40 highest-revision). Agent-side emission compliance is unproven until a paid run; the gate proves the code paths.

amendments.title: Operator redaction rules + may_use_web enforcement + built-but-unwired LAW-IV sensitivity layer

change.phantom_strip: removed the model-judges-sensitivity phantom: REDACT_CLERK's run_objectives no longer says 'screen for sensitive content, redact what warrants it'. The redactors now APPLY operator-declared rules; they do not decide on their own what is sensitive. LAW-IV's own phrase 'content marked for redaction' is the basis for the operator-rule model.
change.conventions_as_redaction_rules: convention_parser gains a 'redact' action and a REDACTION_CATEGORIES set (confidentiality/redaction/privacy/pii); redaction_rules(registry) compiles operator conventions in those categories (or action=redact) into machine-usable rules {id,category,rule,severity,action}, falling back to DEFAULT_REDACTION_RULES (national ID numbers; named individuals; confidential turnover/financial figures; business secrets) when the operator has authored none.
change.redaction_rules_wired: phase_9_redaction computes redaction_rules(convention_registry) and passes them plus the document spans in the REDACT_CLERK work_payload, and threads convention_registry to the clerk; bus_reader gives qwen_local a non-zero conventions budget (800) so the rules actually reach the redactors. The clerk read-radius is minimally unblinded with document_text so a rule can be applied to spans (the full ladder radius is Stage 3b).
change.may_use_web_enforced: may_use_web is now a real, consumed control: search_router loads the agent registry and SearchRouter.search refuses (PermissionError) any roster agent whose may_use_web is false; a system/intake caller (agent=None, e.g. the date cascade) is permitted. Redactors are may_use_web=false and can never be routed to the web. Web-per-redaction-tier is deferred to Stage 3b.
change.sensitivity_layer_built_unwired: scripts/sensitivity_layer.py scaffolds the FULL LAW-IV sensitivity layer (sensitivity as a first-class concept; mask_for_external to strip sensitive content from any API/web boundary; may_handle_sensitive routing) but it is INERT: LAYER_ACTIVE=False, the masking hook is a transparent pass-through, and nothing in control flow consumes it. The dormant on-switch is LAYER_ACTIVE plus wiring the helpers; the may_handle_sensitive registry flags are the routing on-switch.
change.inactive_layer_hard_gate: while the full layer is inactive the pipeline WARNS and REFUSES to start unless the operator passes --sensitivity-layer-inactive-override (interactive confirmation when interactive), each override appended to durable/governance/sensitivity_overrides.jsonl. Mirrors the Qwen redaction --no-redaction-override hard-gate-plus-logged-override pattern and fires on every normal run.
change.deferral: the full sensitivity philosophy is DEFERRED to real-life / full deployment; Stage 3a ships only local operator-rule application. Documented in README and CLAUDE.md.
change.scope_preserved: LAW-IV's seed-law text is cited, NOT modified (byte-for-byte unchanged). INFRA-033 (amendments master), INFRA-037 (canonical envelope) and the message-bus transport envelope are unchanged. Redactors still emit the INFRA-037 wrapper (one redaction per item; items:[] = nothing to redact) and the Stage-1 strict LAW-IV BLOCK behavior is intact.

amendments.reason: The redaction phase previously asked a 7B model to JUDGE what is 'sensitive' (a phantom decision); LAW-IV instead points to operator-marked content. This DELTA makes redaction rule-driven (operator conventions compiled to rules and actually delivered to the redactors), makes may_use_web a real capability gate, and builds the full sensitivity-enforcement layer as inert scaffolding behind a hard gate so the deferral is explicit and conscious rather than silent.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the INFRA-029 amendment tripwire: adding a new id is not a violation; no existing seed law or amendment modified or deleted). LAW-IV (seed law) cited, not touched. Verify gate updated to 44 checks (41 redaction rules, 42 may_use_web enforcement, 43 sensitivity-layer inactive + logged override). Full sensitivity layer and web-per-tier are unwired/deferred; agent emission compliance unproven until a paid run.

amendments.title: Editorial review board (single senior reviewer, stage 1 of staged build)

change.house: Creates the EDITORIAL review house, which was never built (what previously existed under the name 'redaction' was privacy machinery, a false-friend error: English 'redaction' = masking, the operator meant French 'redaction' = editing). The editorial house is privacy-free. It imports NOTHING from scripts/sensitivity_layer/ and reuses no privacy mechanic. No editorial name contains 'redact' in any spelling or any French cognate.
change.roster: Adds exactly ONE agent, EDITOR. backend claude_api; model key claude-opus-4-8 (resolved live via enforce_current_models/resolve_model_id, like LEGAL_ANALYST, never a hardcoded dated id); category editorial; may_use_web false; may_handle_sensitive false. EXPECTED_AGENTS goes 12 -> 13.
change.position: Stated by EXECUTION ORDER, not by label number (labels are not sequential: phase 9 executes before phase 8). EDITOR runs in a new phase labeled 6.5, inserted in execution order immediately AFTER phase_6_synthesis (after AMENDMENT_DRAFTER assembles the canonical master) and BEFORE phase 7 and before the phase 9 privacy scrub. EDITOR reasons over the CLEAN, pre-scrub assembled editorial deliverable, the master at <run>/deliverables/<doc_id>__amendments.json, and never over scrubbed text.
change.job: Senior editorial review of the assembled deliverable's SUBSTANCE and DRAFTING: soundness, internal coherence, necessity, and quality of the amendments and analysis. EDITOR emits editorial observations in the canonical INFRA-037 envelope ({agent, doc_id, items:[flat]}), one observation per item. Each item carries: ref (what it comments on), verdict (from the fixed editorial set), rationale (free-text editorial reasoning in prose), confidence. EDITOR does NOT mask, detect PII, or scrub. Output is ADVISORY to the operator: it annotates; it does NOT modify the deliverable and does NOT gate whether the deliverable ships.
change.editorial_verdict_set: Fixed at stage 1, exactly one of: 'sound' (no editorial concern), 'concern' (editorial issue worth operator attention), 'serious_concern' (substantive soundness/necessity problem the operator should resolve before shipping). This set defines a 'valid editorial verdict' for the silent-pass guard below. No other values are permitted.
change.rationale_field: At stage 1 each observation carries a free-text 'rationale' naming the editorial reasoning in prose. There is NO principle_id at stage 1, because the operator-ratified meta-precedent store that would define principle ids is deferred. When that store lands in a later DELTA, rationale is superseded by or augmented with a principle_id pointing at an operator-ratified principle. No principle_id is wired into a non-existent store now.
change.sensitive_run_gating: Option B, reusing the existing waiver regime (no new regime, and the dormant masking layer stays inactive). EDITOR runs on Claude (an external API) at phase 6.5, UPSTREAM of the phase 9 privacy scrub, so it is an API egress point for pre-scrub content. To keep LAW-IV intact: stage-1 EDITOR runs ONLY on a run declared non-sensitive, i.e. when the SAME --no-redaction-override waiver is in force (recorded by record_redaction_waiver to the governance ledger durable/governance/redaction_waivers.jsonl). On a run NOT declared non-sensitive (no waiver), phase 6.5 EDITOR is SKIPPED, and the skip is recorded loudly in the run summary as 'editorial review skipped: sensitive run, awaiting masking-layer activation' (never a silent omission). Sensitive-mode editorial review is DEFERRED until the LAW-IV masking layer (sensitivity_layer pillars 1+2) is activated; this dependency is recorded explicitly.

borrowed_good_practice.silent_pass_doctrine: EDITOR output that does not parse into items each carrying a VALID editorial verdict (per the fixed set) is a LOUD failure surfaced to the operator as 'editorial review failed' in the run summary. Scope of the failure: because EDITOR is advisory, this failure does NOT halt the pipeline and does NOT withhold the deliverable; it flags that the editorial review itself did not complete, so the operator knows the review is ABSENT rather than silently empty. A genuine 'no concerns' result is items each with verdict 'sound', which is DISTINCT from malformed or absent output.
borrowed_good_practice.structural_detection: An editorial observation is recognized by carrying ref + verdict + rationale, regardless of any free-text label the model attaches.
borrowed_good_practice.raw_output_persisted: EDITOR raw output is persisted on EVERY path, including the all-'sound' path and the skipped-sensitive path.
borrowed_good_practice.cache_loss_detectability: EDITOR uses the existing stable-prefix cache logging like other Claude agents, so a silent prompt-cache loss is visible in the cost log.

change.ordering_enforcement: The execution-order guarantee (EDITOR runs after AMENDMENT_DRAFTER and before the phase 9 privacy scrub, reading the clean master) is enforced by a NEW verify-gate check added in the build pass (not in this constitution object). This DELTA records that the ordering is gate-enforced.

amendments.reason: The civil-service editorial review board the operator intended was never built; the agents previously named REDACT_CLERK/AUTHORITY/GATE were privacy redactors (a false-friend error, now corrected and consolidated into the single privacy REDACTOR inside scripts/sensitivity_layer/, Phase 1c). The editorial house must be created fresh, privacy-free, and correctly named, beginning with a single senior reviewer (EDITOR) that gives the operator an advisory read on the substance and drafting quality of each assembled deliverable. Editorial review is governed structure, so it is ratified here before it is built. It is deliberately staged: stage 1 is one advisory reviewer over the clean master, with the full rank ladder and the meta-precedent store deferred to later DELTAs so they are implemented, not re-litigated.
amendments.note: STAGED FORWARD DESIGN (ratified now so the later DELTA implements without re-litigation): the civil-service RANK LADDER (Clerk, Head of Unit, Head of Section, Head of Department, Deputy Director General, Director General) with a mandate per rank; adaptive UP-escalation; parsimony (most calls resolve at the lowest rank); bounded rounds (operator-set, default 5); the Director General existential gate ('do we need this content at all?'); in-house widening read-scope by rank achieved ONLY through a broader bus/durable read radius (there is NO web at ANY rank, including the Director General; wider vision comes from wider reading, never from the network); and an operator-ratified meta-precedent store of payload-free principles, cross-run, where principle_id is introduced and supersedes the stage-1 free-text rationale. The ladder STRUCTURE may be lifted from the prior privacy ladder design ONLY after being SCRUBBED of all three privacy mechanics, which do NOT transfer: web-radius-per-tier, Qwen read-budget lifting, and span/sensitivity assessment. GOVERNANCE: governed structure (hence this DELTA); the phase is sequential with existing phases; no editorial observation is silently dropped (conserve-or-surface). DEPENDENCY: sensitive-run editorial review is blocked on activation of the LAW-IV masking layer (sensitivity_layer pillars 1+2); until then sensitive runs skip EDITOR loudly. The id INFRA-039 is the next free amendment id (INFRA-038 is the committed highest; the wrong-framing privacy ladder once drafted as 039 was never committed to amendments[] and remains only in stash, so 039 is clean and taking it leaves no INFRA-031 gap).

amendments.title: Editorial review board rank ladder (stage 2)

change.house: Extends the privacy-free EDITORIAL review house created in INFRA-039. The board imports NOTHING from scripts/sensitivity_layer/ and reuses no privacy mechanic. No editorial rank name contains 'redact' in any spelling or any French cognate (the false-friend correction is preserved: English 'redaction' = masking lives only in scripts/sensitivity_layer/; the operator's intended French 'redaction' = editing is this house).
change.roster: The stage-1 EDITOR is RENAMED to EDITOR_CLERK (a total rename across the registry key, the agent_contracts key, the agent_wrapper worked-example name literal, the pipeline dispatch and raw-output filename, and verify check_51 / EXPECTED_AGENTS). Five new ranks are added ABOVE it, in ascending authority: EDITOR_HEAD_OF_UNIT, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_SECTION, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_DEPARTMENT, EDITOR_DEPUTY_DG, EDITOR_DG. All six carry category editorial, may_use_web false, may_handle_sensitive false. EXPECTED_AGENTS goes 13 -> 18.
change.family_split: Decorrelated senior check by model family. Bottom three ranks (EDITOR_CLERK, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_UNIT, EDITOR_HEAD_OF_SECTION) use backend claude_api; top three ranks (EDITOR_HEAD_OF_DEPARTMENT, EDITOR_DEPUTY_DG, EDITOR_DG) use backend openai_api with model key gpt-4o, reusing the EXISTING auditor dispatch path (agent_wrapper.dispatch -> call_gpt, selected purely from spec['backend'] with no name special-casing). Every model id is resolved live via enforce_current_models/resolve_model_id (like LEGAL_ANALYST and the existing GPT auditors); no dated id is ever hardcoded.
change.law_iii_interpretation: LAW-III governs the PRODUCER/AUDITOR relationship (a producer must not audit its own work; the auditor is cross-family). Editorial intra-board escalation is a REVIEW relationship, distinct from that AUDIT relationship: a higher rank reviews a lower rank's editorial observation, it does not audit a producer's deliverable. Therefore same-family lower-rank escalation (within the Claude trio) is PERMITTED and is not a LAW-III violation. The cross-family boundary at the top (Claude trio -> GPT trio) is applied as decorrelation BEST PRACTICE for a senior independent check, NOT as a LAW-III mandate. This interpretation is recorded so the family split is understood as design, not as a claimed LAW-III requirement.
change.position: Unchanged execution slot from INFRA-039: the whole board runs in phase 6.5, in execution order AFTER phase_6_synthesis (after AMENDMENT_DRAFTER assembles the canonical master) and BEFORE phase 7 and BEFORE the phase 9 privacy scrub. The board reads the CLEAN, pre-scrub assembled master at <run>/deliverables/<doc_id>__amendments.json. The board is ADVISORY: it annotates only; it never modifies the master and never gates whether the deliverable ships.
change.escalation: A call resolves at the LOWEST competent rank (parsimony: most calls resolve at EDITOR_CLERK and never summon a higher rank). A higher rank is summoned by one of two operator-tunable triggers: (a) the lower rank's confidence falls below an operator-set threshold, or (b) the lower rank raises an explicit out-of-mandate flag. A summoned higher rank reads the lower rank's observation AND its rationale (accumulating state) and then confirms, overrides, or escalates further up the ladder. Authority is tied to RANK, not to model family: a higher rank's verdict GOVERNS the outcome regardless of which family it runs on (the family split is decorrelation, not an authority distinction). An override does NOT delete the lower rank's observation; BOTH persist on the bus (the lower rank's original observation and rationale, plus the higher rank's superseding verdict), preserving conserve-or-surface. The lower rank's contribution remains on record even when overruled.
change.per_rank_mandate: Scope widens with rank, but NO rank reaches the web (may_use_web false at every rank including EDITOR_DG); 'broader vision' means a wider read of the message bus and durable assets, never external egress. EDITOR_CLERK + EDITOR_HEAD_OF_UNIT + EDITOR_HEAD_OF_SECTION: editorial review of drafting and soundness at provision-and-neighbors scope. EDITOR_HEAD_OF_DEPARTMENT: whole-deliverable coherence. EDITOR_DEPUTY_DG: necessity and proportionality. EDITOR_DG: the existential question ('do we need this content at all?'), fired ONLY when EDITOR_DG is summoned.
change.bounded_loop: The ONE new mechanism: rank-to-rank escalation is NEW intra-phase control flow on the message bus. It MUST NOT reuse the operator-escalation ESCALATE path (orchestrator.escalate_to_operator, which posts UNRESOLVED to OPERATOR and blocks on _collect_operator_decision). The loop is governed by the three-pillar loop test: (1) external verification — the summoned rank is a higher, and at the top a cross-family, reviewer; (2) accumulating state — each rank's observation and rationale persist on the bus as the loop climbs, never recomputed from scratch; (3) bounded stop — an operator-set max_rounds (default 5) lives in a NEW versioned-JSON config tunable, e.g. config/editorial_board.json, following the existing versioned-config convention. The confidence-below-threshold summon trigger has an explicit operator-tunable default: a rank escalates when its confidence is below 0.7 (operator-adjustable in config/editorial_board.json), so the build does not invent a default silently. After the cap the board renders a TERMINAL decision and never climbs further (no infinite climb). Conserve-or-surface: no rank's observation is ever silently dropped.
change.verdict_set: Unchanged from stage 1: exactly one of {sound, concern, serious_concern}. The stage-1 free-text rationale per observation is unchanged. principle_id remains DEFERRED to the separate meta-precedent DELTA and is not wired into any non-existent store now.
change.sensitive_run_gating: Unchanged Option B, reusing the existing waiver regime. The WHOLE board (both the Claude ranks and the GPT ranks) runs ONLY on a run declared non-sensitive, i.e. when the --no-redaction-override waiver is in force (recorded to durable/governance/redaction_waivers.jsonl). The top-three GPT ranks are an ADDITIONAL external egress beyond the stage-1 single Claude egress, so the whole-board gate matters MORE here than it did at stage 1. On a run not declared non-sensitive the entire board is SKIPPED and the skip is recorded LOUDLY in the run summary (never a silent omission). Sensitive-mode editorial review remains DEFERRED until the LAW-IV masking layer (sensitivity_layer pillars 1+2) is activated.

borrowed_good_practice.silent_pass_doctrine: Carried from stage 1 and applied per rank: any rank's output that does not parse into items each carrying a VALID editorial verdict is a LOUD failure surfaced as 'editorial review failed' in the run summary. Because the board is advisory, the failure does NOT halt the pipeline and does NOT withhold the deliverable; it flags that the editorial review itself did not complete, so the operator knows the review is ABSENT rather than silently empty.
borrowed_good_practice.structural_detection: An editorial observation is recognized by carrying ref + verdict + rationale, regardless of any free-text label the model attaches.
borrowed_good_practice.raw_output_persisted: Raw output is persisted on EVERY path (normal, all-sound, skipped-sensitive) AND per rank, so each rank's contribution is independently auditable.
borrowed_good_practice.cache_loss_detectability: Each Claude rank uses the existing stable-prefix cache logging, so a silent prompt-cache loss remains visible in the cost log.

change.gates: check_51 generalizes from one agent to six and becomes per-rank-aware: it asserts the FAMILY SPLIT itself (bottom three claude_api, top three openai_api) and that all six ranks are category editorial, may_use_web false, may_handle_sensitive false, import nothing from sensitivity_layer, and constrain verdict to exactly {sound, concern, serious_concern}. check_52 ordering still holds for the whole board phase (board after AMENDMENT_DRAFTER, before phase 7 and the phase 9 scrub, reading the clean master). NEW checks are added in the build pass (NOT in this constitution object): the bounded-rounds cap is enforced, and rank-to-rank escalation does NOT use the operator ESCALATE path. The cost projection is labeled a WORST-CASE ceiling (all six ranks x num_op_docs, split by family) with an expected-case note (parsimony: typically EDITOR_CLERK only). NOTE: this object is ratified at INFRA-040 BUILD A, which performs only the rename, the five new rank agents, and the 13->18 count; the escalation loop, the config/editorial_board.json tunable, and the full check_51 family-split generalization land in subsequent build passes (B and C). BUILD A leaves check_51 pointed at EDITOR_CLERK as a minimal green-keeping placeholder.
change.staged_build_and_proof: Built staged on the proven EDITOR_CLERK (the renamed stage-1 reviewer). Two proof runs are required before the board is trusted: one exercising a Claude upper rank, and one exercising a GPT rank (GPT has only ever AUDITED, never EDITED; the GPT proof must demonstrate real editorial judgment, not audit behavior).
change.governance: Editorial review is governed structure, so this rank ladder is ratified here before it is built. The meta-precedent store (principle_id; operator-ratified, payload-free principles) remains a SEPARATE later DELTA and is not introduced by this object.

amendments.reason: INFRA-039 created the editorial house with a single advisory reviewer as stage 1 of a deliberately staged build. Stage 2 installs the civil-service rank ladder the operator intended: the proven reviewer becomes EDITOR_CLERK and five senior ranks are added above it, with escalation that resolves at the lowest competent rank and climbs only when confidence is low or a matter is out of mandate. The ranks are split across two model families (Claude trio below, GPT trio above) for a decorrelated senior check, reusing the existing auditor GPT dispatch path with all model ids resolved live. The board stays advisory, privacy-free, and confined to phase 6.5 over the clean master. The single genuinely new mechanism is a bounded rank-to-rank escalation loop on the message bus, governed by an external-verification / accumulating-state / bounded-stop test and explicitly forbidden from reusing the operator-escalation ESCALATE path. It is ratified before it is built so the structure is implemented, not re-litigated.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the INFRA-029 amendment tripwire: adding a new id is not a violation; no existing seed law or amendment is modified or deleted). LAW-III (seed law) is cited and interpreted, NOT modified: editorial intra-board escalation is a REVIEW relationship distinct from the producer/auditor AUDIT relationship LAW-III governs, so same-family lower-rank escalation is permitted and the cross-family top is best practice, not a LAW-III mandate. Authority is by RANK, not family; an override supersedes but never deletes the lower rank's observation (both persist on the bus). EXPECTED_AGENTS 13 -> 18 (EDITOR renamed to EDITOR_CLERK + five new ranks). A NEW versioned config config/editorial_board.json carries the operator tunables: max_rounds (default 5), the confidence-escalation threshold (default 0.7 — a rank escalates when its confidence is below 0.7), and the out-of-mandate trigger. Verify gate to be updated across build passes (check_51 generalized to six ranks and family-split-aware; check_52 ordering for the whole board; plus new checks for the bounded-rounds cap and for escalation NOT using the operator ESCALATE path). BUILD A (this pass) does the rename + five rank agents + 13->18 count only; the escalation loop, the config tunable, and the check_51 generalization are BUILD B/C. The whole board runs only on a --no-redaction-override declared-non-sensitive run; the top-three GPT ranks are an additional external egress, so the whole-board sensitive-run gate matters more here. principle_id and the meta-precedent store remain deferred to a separate later DELTA. Agent-side editorial-judgment compliance (especially the GPT ranks, which have only ever audited) is unproven until the two required proof runs; this object ratifies the governed structure, the build pass proves the code paths. BUILD F (output budget): the per-rank output budget was found truncating upper ranks (which re-review ALL accumulated lower-rank observations, so their output grows with rank) under the inherited stage-1 max_tokens=2048, which surfaced as a LOUD EDITORIAL_FAILED on every escalation (the silent-pass doctrine worked, refusing to ship truncated output); fixed by making max_tokens an operator tunable in config/editorial_board.json (default 8192) resolved like the other knobs, with a regression-catching gate check (no hardcoded 2048). Both paid proof runs passed: a Claude upper rank (EDITOR_HEAD_OF_SECTION) and a GPT rank (EDITOR_HEAD_OF_DEPARTMENT) produced valid editorial judgment (coherence/necessity/ordering/register reasoning, not audit). KNOWN RESIDUAL (logged for the record, NOT a defect and NOT fixed in this pass): the GPT ranks produce correct editorial reasoning but SHALLOWER than the Claude opus ranks (less specific, fewer source anchors) — an accepted quality characteristic of the cross-family decorrelation split, to be revisited (model/prompt) only by a future operator-ratified change, never silently.

amendments.title: LAW-IV outbound masking protocol (full sensitivity layer activation + payload-free cross-run stores)

change.law: Activates the full LAW-IV sensitivity layer (Mechanism 2, previously dormant at LAYER_ACTIVE=False) as a real outbound MASKING PROTOCOL. The protocol is an x/y split applied to every item that would cross an external boundary (any API call or web request): x = non-sensitive items, passed through unchanged; y = sensitive items, HELD LOCAL and replaced in the outbound payload by a typed placeholder [REDACTED:TYPE] carrying only the field TYPE, never the content. Sensitivity is OPERATOR-DEFINED, never model-judged: the y set is exactly what the operator's compiled conventions mark, via the existing scripts/sensitivity_layer/rules.py compile path and the redaction_detect deterministic operator-authorized detector; no new sensitivity judge is invented (INFRA-038 lineage). Each item carries a per-item EXPOSURE TAG (passed for x, masked for y, with the placeholder field names). After the external call the held-local y content is rejoined to the response by the INFRA-037 canonical keys (item_id + revision) and deduped (highest revision wins). Every masking decision is appended to a per-item EXPOSURE LEDGER under durable/governance (append-only, survives reset, never raw content): this ledger is the LAW-IV audit trail proving no sensitive span left the machine. LAW-IV is CITED and ENACTED, not modified.
change.chokepoints: The protocol engages at the FOUR egress chokepoints found in the audit, sensitive mode only, network paths only: (1) the per-agent API call (agent_wrapper.run_task/dispatch), UPSTREAM of build_prompt, for the claude_api and openai_api backends ONLY (qwen_local is local hardware and is EXEMPT: sensitive content is permitted to reach the local model, the purpose of may_handle_sensitive routing); (2) search_router.search (the web query path); (3) the claim/verification path (claim_classifier claim assembly plus the VERIFIER/FACT_CHECKER source_text / source_excerpt / processor_draft payloads); (4) document_dating.date_from_web, the BOOT web egress that today can send an operator document title to the web. At chokepoint 4 the safe action is to SUPPRESS the web call under sensitive mode (a masked title is meaningless for a date search) and fall back to the local filename/metadata/text cascade. may_handle_sensitive becomes the LIVE routing consumer at these chokepoints (previously a zero-caller flag).
change.boot_stores_option_b: The BOOT learning/reference stores are made payload-free BY CONSTRUCTION (Option B: re-architect WHAT is stored, not mask-after), because adaptive_spawn and document_dating both ingest the operator's input/context/ case documents. Changes: (a) citation_convention.json stores the matched pattern id plus sample count and DROPS the verbatim substring examples; (b) situational_awareness.md and linguistic_identity.md store institution CATEGORIES not verbatim names and DROP the verbatim quoted representative sentences; (c) document_dates.json stores filename plus date (and date_source/date_confidence) only and DROPS title-from-content and abs_path. speech_acts_taxonomy.json is unchanged (generic verb forms, not operator spans). The abstracted stores must stay USEFUL and must NOT hold a verbatim operator span in ANY mode (by construction, not mode-gated); downstream readers (ontology_graph build_graph ingest, situational consumers) must still build.
change.cross_run_gaps: Two cross-run store gaps are closed, reusing the P1 mask path (no second masker is forked): (a) ontology_graph.build_graph gains a sensitive parameter and masks Convention.rule (Q5) and CitationForm.examples (Q6) under sensitive mode, real content under non-sensitive; (b) ontology_capture delta_proposals gating is extended from evidence-only to ALSO mask trigger and proposed_change under sensitive mode. B1 provisions and B3 gnn_state are already payload-free and are unchanged.
change.closure_condition: Every scaffold part that was built-but-dormant ends this DELTA with a LIVE DUTY, gate-proven, with no dormant-but-claimed-built scaffold remaining: mask_for_external gets a real implementation AND live callers at the four chokepoints (was a zero-caller pass-through stub); may_handle_sensitive becomes the live routing consumer (was a zero-caller flag); LAYER_ACTIVE/is_active gate the protocol on; the exposure ledger has a real writer. A standing closure check applies after every part: account for every new or touched function, flag, field, branch, and store against a live caller or executed gate path; flag anything with zero duty.
change.gates: Each part lands its own executed-coverage checks (the WIRE-AT-THE-END discipline; non-mutating, tempdir). P1: mask_for_external/mask_exchange produce typed placeholders for y, pass x, write the per-item ledger, rejoin and dedupe by item_id/revision, and are idempotent on already-masked input. P2: each of the four chokepoints masks or withholds under sensitive mode and passes raw under non-sensitive; the qwen_local path is proven EXEMPT; chokepoint 4 is proven not to send a raw title under sensitive mode. P3: the BOOT stores contain no verbatim operator span post-BOOT on a synthetic corpus, and downstream ingest still builds. P4: graph.json masks rule plus examples under sensitive mode (real under non-sensitive); delta_proposals masks evidence, trigger, and proposed_change under sensitive mode. P5 (paid, operator-go-only): one real activated sensitive run proving end-to-end masking at all four chokepoints, the per-step hard gate, the per-item ledger, all stores payload-free, and no raw operator span reaching any API, web, or cross-run store.
change.build_sequence: Built in five sequenced parts, each committed standalone with the gate green and non-mutating: P1 masking engine; P2 wire the four chokepoints; P3 Option-B BOOT stores; P4 close the two cross-run gaps; P5 deploy-then-test (the only paid step, run only on explicit operator go). This DELTA moves the full sensitivity layer from BUILT-BUT-UNWIRED to BUILT-AND-WIRED; the inactive-layer hard gate (require the override waiver) remains the refuse-to-start posture until the layer is proven active in P5.
change.governance: This object ratifies the governed structure before it is built (the INFRA-040 staged-build precedent). The build passes prove the code paths. principle_id and the meta-precedent store remain deferred to their separate DELTA and are not introduced here.

amendments.reason: The audit found the full LAW-IV sensitivity layer is a scaffold, not an implementation: mask_for_external was a zero-caller pass-through stub, may_handle_sensitive a zero-caller flag, all four egress chokepoints sent raw operator content, the BOOT learning stores were operator-content-derived (citation examples, quoted sentences, document titles, abs_path), and two cross-run stores (graph.json convention.rule plus citation examples, delta_proposals trigger plus proposed_change) persisted raw spans. This DELTA closes that leak surface as a real outbound masking protocol grounded in operator conventions (never a model sensitivity judge), gives both dormant scaffold parts a live gate-proven duty, makes the BOOT stores payload-free by construction, and proves the whole thing end-to-end on one activated sensitive run. It is ratified before it is built so the masking law is implemented, not re-litigated.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the INFRA-029 amendment tripwire: adding a new id is not a violation; no seed law or existing amendment is modified or deleted). The per-item exposure ledger (durable/governance/exposure_ledger.jsonl) is the LAW-IV audit trail and carries no raw content. principle_id and the meta-precedent store remain deferred to their separate DELTA. Built in sequenced parts P1..P5; P1 (this pass) builds the masking engine (mask_for_external/mask_exchange/rejoin_after_external) with executed-coverage gate checks; wiring and the remaining parts follow.

amendments.title: Empty-convention citation regime + WEB-REF as a backed citation form

change.empty_convention_carveout: Carve-out to the Part XVIII Section D / checklist-35 rule (genesis.md line 1434, 'An amendment without at least one CONV-* and one REF-* is a contract violation', and checklist item 35 at line 1554), directly analogous to the Part XXIII document-level location carve-out. WHEN the convention registry is empty (the existing convention_review_enabled=False signal, i.e. the conventions list is empty or absent), an amendment grounded by at least one REF-* OR at least one WEB-REF-* is VALID and is NOT flagged with a spurious missing-CONV error, and convention_ref is not required. This is the ONLY state in which the CONV-* requirement is relaxed. When conventions exist the rule holds UNCHANGED (at least one CONV-* AND at least one REF-*, convention_ref required). Rationale: with zero conventions in existence a CONV-* citation is unsatisfiable, so the finding grounds in retrieved context (REF-*) or a discovered web reference (WEB-REF-*) instead.
change.web_ref_backed: WEB-REF, today only Part XX prose (genesis.md line 1630: discovered references are cited with full URL, title, issuing body, year, and marked as [WEB-REF] to distinguish them from corpus references [REF-*]), becomes a REAL structured citation form: a monotonic WEB-REF-NNNN id minted and persisted by the per-run reference index (parallel to REF-NNNN, in a web_references list), carrying url, title, issuing_body, year, and citable in the ref_ids array exactly as a REF-*. The citation validators accept WEB-REF-* as a grounding form. WEB-REF ids are minted from the STRUCTURED web-source fields only: FACT_CHECKER source_url, PRACTICE_AUDITOR reference_url, and PRACTICE_AUDITOR reference_source. Those raw fields remain a transitional fallback.
change.scope_boundary: WEB-REF covers every web reference carried in a STRUCTURED field (source_url, reference_url, reference_source), which is the complete set in the empty-registry regime this DELTA addresses. INLINE free-text URLs and inline [WEB-REF] markings (in evidence, recommendation, reasoning, comment) are OUT OF SCOPE: Part XX inline web discovery is convention-activated and does not fire in the empty-registry state, so inline extraction is deferred to a separate later build if convention-driven web discovery is live and real use shows inline URLs slipping through. No universality is claimed.
change.regex_disambiguation: The corpus-REF detector is tightened to (?<!WEB-)\bREF-\d{4,}\b so a WEB-REF-NNNN id is never accidentally matched as a REF; a WEB-REF detector \bWEB-REF-\d{4,}\b is added. Applied consistently in the amendment validator and the OPT-1 verifiability gate.
change.opt1_consistency: The OPT-1 verifiability gate is_grounded recognizes a WEB-REF-* id as grounding (with the raw source_url / reference_url / reference_source clause kept as fallback), so OPT-1 and this carve-out agree on what grounded means.
change.scope: Pipeline behavior plus this governed carve-out. No seed law is touched. The relaxation is state-gated (empty registry only) and never blanket. Inline web-reference extraction is explicitly deferred. principle_id and other deferred items are untouched.

amendments.reason: Empty-registry runs currently ship amendments carrying a spurious missing-CONV validator error, because the CONV-* requirement is unconditional while zero conventions exist to cite (the cold-battery state). This DELTA relaxes the CONV requirement ONLY in the empty state, grounding amendments in retrieved context (REF-*) or discovered web references (WEB-REF-*), and promotes WEB-REF from Part XX prose to a backed, citable form minted from the three structured web-source fields. Inline free-text URL extraction is deferred as a separate convention-activated concern that does not arise in the empty-registry regime. It is a governed carve-out analogous to the Part XXIII document-level carve-out, so it is ratified before it is built.
amendments.note: Append-only DELTA (allowed by the INFRA-029 amendment tripwire; no seed law or existing amendment modified or deleted). Relaxes a governed genesis rule (Part XVIII Section D + checklist 35 + check_35) for the empty-registry state ONLY; unchanged when conventions exist. Backs Part XX WEB-REF prose with real structure, minted from FACT_CHECKER source_url + PRACTICE_AUDITOR reference_url + PRACTICE_AUDITOR reference_source (structured fields only; inline free-text out of scope, no universality claimed). Proposal-side, operator-ratified, does not self-apply, under the meta-law tripwire. The build (PART 2.2) implements the reference-builder WEB-REF minting/persistence, the three-field mint pass, the registry-empty-aware validator, the OPT-1 is_grounded reconciliation, the contract-field declaration, and the regex disambiguation, with executed-coverage gate checks; built only after this DELTA is ratified.
